newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds surge ahead, spreads wider.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds surge ahead, spreads wider.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities climbed swiftly Thursday afternoon in the wake of a fair 30-year Treasury bond auction.
Pass-through yield spreads kept pace with Treasuries most of the trading session, but widened by a whisker late in the day, traders said.
"Yesterday, there were some decent flows in mortgages but they seem to be pretty well-absorbed," said one trader at a large Midwest investment firm.
Today, mortgage spreads are "right in line" with their counterparts, he said.
By late afternoon, mortgage-backeds were 2/32 to 12/32 higher in most coupons, while comparable Treasuries were 9/32 to 15/32 higher.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent issues were 11/32 higher, at 100-24/32, yielding 104 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was up 11/32 as well, at 100-18/32 and 100-23/32, respectively. The 10-year Treasury bond was up 15/32 to yield 6.31 percent.
In its final leg of its quarterly refunding, the Treasury auctioned about $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
Analysts called the results of the auction "not terrible, but not great either."
"Lots of people (were) talking about the auction," one trader said, adding "not many people participating."
Friday's abbreviated trading session coupled with next week's economic data schedule may bring more retail activity to the Treasury market, he said.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended an early close at 1400 EST/1900 GMT Friday for U.S. credit markets, and a full close on Monday.
